discovery: Twist-angle engineering of van der Waals bilayers: prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University / Applied Materials, Israel

motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that a small rotation between two graphene sheets makes the moiré Dirac bands nearly flat at a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this by building such devices and finding correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in one tunable, atomically thin system. This made the twist angle a new control parameter, and in my view it is the purest case of crystal geometry being used as a design variable. 'Twistronics' then grew into a whole field. It includes orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, fractional Chern insulators in moiré TMDs, and moiré ferroelectrics. All of these come from the same mechanism of using stacking and rotation to create strong correlations on demand. The discovery changed how condensed-matter physicists study strongly correlated electrons, and it opened new routes to quantum and electronic devices.
